knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Spraying a cloth keeps liquid away from the controls and vents, which must stay dry.
The tray is removed so that it can be washed on its own and the floor beneath it can be reached.
A soft cloth with a gentle cleaner, wiped along the grain, protects a stainless finish from marks.

practicalCriteria: Removes and cleans the tray separately before cleaning the cavity.
Sprays the cloth, not the controls or vents, during exterior and control cleaning.
Checks the interior for residue before the microwave is returned to use.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. The practical sign-off is separate, observed by an assessor, and is not shown by a quiz result.
evidenceRequired: Observed practical sign-off on assessor sheet
Job record or photo of the finished area
stopWorkCriteria: Liquid applied to vents, openings or controls
Unit opened or a panel removed
Coarse scourer used on a stainless finish
